title: Human escalation policy (escalation-policy.yaml)
description: What a failure's severity is allowed to do without a person (T40). Severity has been carried in every StructuredFailure since T06 and read by nothing; this is what gives it a consequence. The runtime authority is DEFAULT_ESCALATION_POLICY in orchestrator/src/escalation/escalationPolicy.ts — a policy that had to be read off disk to decide a retry would fail closed at the worst moment — and --check-escalation-policy fails when the two disagree.

version.description: Schema generation of this file. Bumped only when a change would break an existing reader.

severity.description: One entry per severity in StructuredFailureSchema. All four must be present: a missing severity would be a failure class with no stated policy, which is exactly the state T40 exists to end.

autonomous.description: May the orchestrator retry this by itself at all? False means every occurrence stops for a person, however retryable the failure claims to be.

max_retry.description: Automatic rounds this severity gets, at most. The global ceiling (MAX_RETRY) still outranks it, so this can only ever be stricter — never a way to buy extra rounds.

approval.description: When it stops, is a person formally asked — an approval record with a type and a reason — rather than the task going quiet in BLOCKED?

stop_pipeline.description: Stop the task outright instead of routing the failure to an owner. Stopping is always ESCALATE (a person can answer and the task continues), never ABORT, which is reserved for a spent global budget.

why.description: Why this severity gets this treatment, specifically. Optional but strongly expected: a policy with no reason is one nobody can evaluate an exception against.
